title: The Field-Line Detective
summary: Hunt for faults in field-line pictures, read charges from the lines and predict which released charges follow them.
subject: physics
learningOutcome: The student can spot an impossible field-line diagram and say which rule it breaks, read signs and sizes from a picture, compare field strengths by line density, and say when a charge follows a line.

levels.title: Spot the fault
levels.adds: Baseline: field lines are continuous, never cross, never close up and point from + to − (Ex 1.7). Find the fault and the rule.
hints: Check each rule in turn: do two lines cross? Does a line stop in empty space? Is there a closed loop? Do all arrows run from + to −?
At a crossing the field would have two directions at one point, which is impossible.
Lines start on positive charges (or come from far away) and end on negative ones (or run off).

levels.title: Read the picture
levels.adds: New idea: the arrows tell you the signs and the number of lines at each charge tells you its relative size.
hints: Lines leave a positive charge and arrive on a negative one.
Count the lines that touch each charge: twice the lines means twice the charge.
When one of two opposite charges is larger, some of its lines have no partner and run off to infinity.

levels.title: Compare the strength
levels.adds: New idea: closely packed lines mean a strong field. Rank three points by how crowded the lines are.
hints: The field is stronger where lines are closer together.
Near a charge the lines are crowded, far away they spread out.
Between two opposite charges the lines are packed along the axis.

levels.title: Does it follow the line?
levels.adds: New idea: a charge released from rest follows a field line only where the line is straight, because it has inertia.
hints: A field line shows the direction of the force at each point, not the path of a moving charge.
Where a line curves, the charge keeps going in its old direction and swings off the line.
On the straight line through two charges, the lines are straight, so the charge stays on them.

misconceptions: Field lines are the paths of charges
Field lines can cross where two fields meet
A line can stop anywhere in space
More lines mean a bigger charge in every picture, not just within one picture
